title: Add GitHub Pages deployment workflow
body:
Build the Vite bundle on every push to main and publish it to GitHub Pages
via the official Pages actions — no gh-pages branch and no secrets needed.

The bundle needs no base-path rewrite: vite.config.js already sets
`base: './'` and every asset URL in the source is relative, so the same
dist/ works under /<repo>/ as well as at a domain root.

Also document the one manual step (Settings -> Pages -> Source: GitHub
Actions) and link the demo from the README header.

title: Remove the GitHub Pages deployment
body:
Reverts what PR #1 added, since the project is no longer being published.

## What this removes

- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — the build-and-publish workflow (the `.github/` directory goes with it, as it held nothing else)
- The **Live demo →** link in the README header, which pointed at a URL that resolves to nothing
- The README's `### Deploying` section

PR #1 was purely additive (66 insertions, 0 deletions across two files), so reverting it restores the exact pre-deployment state. `README.md` is now byte-identical to its version in the initial commit; no source file, `vite.config.js` or `package.json` is touched, and the build is unaffected.

## Why

The workflow never succeeded. Both runs failed at `configure-pages` with `Get Pages site failed … Not Found` — the build itself passed every time, but the repository had no Pages site to publish to. Left on `main`, it would keep running and failing on every push.

## Nothing is being taken down

Pages was never enabled, and both runs failed before the deploy job, so no site was ever published and no URL stops working as a result of this.
